audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: The classification (dominant set only: initial primary, default odd-count secondary stress placement coded per word length as 10 100 1010 10100 (1 = a stressed syllable) window 2-5, outside the strict set as morphology-conditioned) rests on Breen 1981:25, the only and best available description of this extinct language, held at page-image grade and re-verified now (PDF p.5 = printed p.25; quotation verbatim). The page supports the classification as the deep note framed it: primary stress 'almost always' initial; secondary hedged ('occasionally', 'may', 'tends') and morphology-first in longer words (bound-morpheme clause outranks odd-count clause; ikalamundu 10010 vs wanatjungkari 10100 at 5 syllables), one exceptional word purinkir with second-syllable main stress. Nothing found suggests a better source exists. The weakness is record hygiene, not sourcing: the catalog row carries empty quote/cite/loc/grade fields and no 'sources' entry even though the note and held scan supp
